verses.english: “Mendicants, suppose there was a boil that was many years old.

verses.pali: Tassassu gaṇḍassa nava vaṇamukhāni nava abhedanamukhāni.
verses.english: And that boil had nine orifices that were continually open wounds.

verses.pali: asuciyeva pagghareyya, duggandhaṁyeva pagghareyya, jegucchiyaṁyeva pagghareyya;
verses.english: would be filthy, stinking, and disgusting.

verses.pali: asuciyeva pasaveyya, duggandhaṁyeva pasaveyya, jegucchiyaṁyeva pasaveyya.
verses.english: would be filthy, stinking, and disgusting.

verses.pali: Gaṇḍoti kho, bhikkhave, imassetaṁ cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa adhivacanaṁ mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṁsanadhammassa.
verses.english: ‘Boil’ is a term for this body made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.

verses.pali: Tassassu gaṇḍassa nava vaṇamukhāni nava abhedanamukhāni.
verses.english: And that boil has nine orifices that are continually open wounds.

verses.pali: asuciyeva paggharati, duggandhaṁyeva paggharati, jegucchiyaṁyeva paggharati;
asuciyeva pasavati, duggandhaṁyeva pasavati, jegucchiyaṁyeva pasavati.

verses.english: So, mendicants, have no illusion about this body.”
